definition: what separates a cued response that automates from a sequence of mine that does not

settled:
Both are action. Only the cued response ever goes automatic.

Two things tell them apart. Following a sequence always feels like work, and I can run two responsive tasks at once but not two sequenced ones correctly.

And a sequence always leaves me somewhere to turn aside. I try variations on one far more than I have seen other people do, which refines the thing and costs more.

Driving is the clean case. The responsive half automates, so I can drive and forget I am driving. The navigation is a sequence and never automates, so on autopilot I often do not arrive where I meant to go.

Nothing substitutes for it. A run of words can be carried by cues, each one firing the next, and I have memorised whole books that way faster than most. It does not carry over to movement, where the cues are neither discrete nor reliably distinct.

So the answer for a sequence of mine is putting it outside me rather than making it automatic.

title: Why A Sequence Never Goes Automatic
